question: This giant mosque by the ocean is in which Moroccan city?
fact: Its minaret is about 210 metres tall, one of the tallest in the world.

question: Jemaa el-Fnaa, the square full of storytellers, music and food stalls, is in which city?
fact: UNESCO protects the traditions of this square as world heritage.

question: Which Moroccan town is famous for its blue painted streets?
fact: Chefchaouen sits in the Rif mountains and is called the Blue Pearl.

question: The oldest university still running in the world, founded in 859, is in which city?
fact: It was founded by a woman, Fatima al-Fihri.

question: What is a tagine?
options: A clay pot and the dish cooked in it
fact: The tall cone lid keeps the food juicy while it cooks slowly.

question: Which famous Moroccan clay village near Ouarzazate appears in many Hollywood movies?
fact: Gladiator and Game of Thrones were filmed there.

question: The ancient Roman city of Volubilis is near which Moroccan city?
fact: Volubilis was an important Roman town 2,000 years ago.

question: What is the famous traditional drink served to guests in Morocco?
fact: It is poured from high up to make foam on top.

question: Which famous explorer from Tangier travelled for about 30 years across Africa and Asia?
fact: He travelled even farther than Marco Polo.

question: Gibraltar is named after Tariq ibn Ziyad. What does Jabal Tariq mean?
fact: Tariq crossed from North Africa to Spain in the year 711.

question: On which day do many Moroccan families eat couscous together?
fact: Couscous is on UNESCO's list of world cultural heritage.

question: What is the highest mountain in North Africa, found in Morocco?
fact: Toubkal in the Atlas mountains is 4,167 metres high.

question: At the 2022 World Cup, Morocco became the first African team to reach which stage?
fact: The Atlas Lions beat Spain and Portugal on the way.

question: What are the native people of North Africa called, whose language is official in Morocco?
fact: Tamazight became an official language of Morocco in 2011.

question: Which ancient wonder of the world is still standing in Egypt today?
fact: It is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.

question: The Great Sphinx has the body of a lion and the head of a...?
fact: It is one of the largest statues ever carved from one rock.

question: Which young pharaoh's tomb was found almost untouched in 1922?
fact: His famous golden mask weighs about 10 kilograms.

question: Which river gave life to ancient Egypt?
fact: The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the world.

question: Which pharaoh built the giant temples of Abu Simbel?
fact: In the 1960s the temples were moved block by block to save them from a lake.

question: Which stone helped experts finally read Egyptian hieroglyphs?
fact: It has the same text written in three scripts.

question: Cleopatra was the last active ruler of which dynasty?
fact: After Cleopatra died in 30 BC, Egypt became part of Rome.

question: Which Egyptian street food mixes rice, pasta, lentils and tomato sauce?
fact: Koshari is often called Egypt's national dish.

question: Where were many pharaohs, including Tutankhamun, buried?
fact: More than 60 tombs have been found there.

question: Which canal in Egypt connects the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea?
fact: It opened in 1869 and ships no longer had to sail around Africa.

question: Which legendary Egyptian singer was called the Star of the East?
fact: Millions across the Arab world listened to her monthly concerts on the radio.

question: Which Egyptian football star is nicknamed the Egyptian King?
fact: Salah became a legend at Liverpool.

question: Which Egyptian city had the most famous library of the ancient world?
fact: A new great library opened there in 2002.

question: Karnak, one of the largest temple complexes ever built, is in which city?
fact: It was built and expanded over about 2,000 years.
